subject: Phased sync + convertible-burst renewal proposal
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@cloudedge.io>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 May 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal and scale — looking for options

Priya,

Hope you’re well. Our exec team is starting renewal planning for the account renewal that comes up Jan 31, 2029. We expect a material uptick next year as we consolidate inference workloads onto fewer vendors. Rough numbers: baseline steady-state tokens projected to grow 2.2x by Q4 2029, with occasional burst windows during product launches (10–72 hour windows).

Primary asks:
- Can Redwood support a multi-year structure that lets us scale capacity year-over-year without renegotiating every quarter?
- We want co-terming with our existing enterprise agreement (ends 2029-01-31).
- Would like an auto-renew option but need an opt-out window and clear notice periods.

Happy to share a basic forecast. We’re flexible on prepay vs annualized billing but need predictability for finance and a burst approach that doesn’t require permanent reserved GPUs.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Gupta
VP, Cloud Platform
CloudEdge
[Attachment: forecast_rough.csv (csv, 12KB)]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@cloudedge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 May 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal and scale — looking for options

Samir — thanks for the clear ask and the early heads up.

High level: we can structure a hybrid renewal that combines multi-year committed capacity for baseline needs plus a \"convertible burst\" allowance — credits you can consume for launches and optionally convert into permanent capacity if you hit sustained utilization thresholds. That should cover predictable budgeting while avoiding over-reserving GPUs.

What I need from you to draft a term sheet:
- 12–24 month horizon you’d consider for the committed piece
- Quarterly forecast numbers (Q3/Q4 2028 + FY29 forecast) — helps us size baseline vs burst credits
- Any strict billing preference (annualized invoice vs monthly true-up)

I’m looping in Marissa (AM) and Ben (SE) to propose pricing and technical guardrails. I’ll prepare a first-pass term sheet and a short appendix explaining the conversion thresholds and auto-renew notice window.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_term_sheet_v1.pdf (pdf, 42KB)]

From: Samir Gupta <samir@cloudedge.io>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@cloudedge.io, legal@cloudedge.io
Date: Thu, 3 May 2028 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal and scale — looking for options

Thanks Priya. Quick answers:
- We can commit on a 24-month structure if pricing is favorable.
- Sending a cleaned forecast attached (Q3–Q4 2028 + FY29) — baseline vs anticipated launch spikes called out.
- Preference: annualized billing with a quarterly true-up for overages.

Two legal asks up front:
1) Auto-renew: 60-day opt-out notice before renewal date, and a 90-day notice for material SLA changes.
2) Data residency and audit rights — need KMS attestation for logs retained beyond 90 days.

If you can show how the convertible-burst would convert into committed capacity (thresholds, lookback window), we can model finance impact quickly.

Samir
[Attachment: cloudedge_forecast_q3q4_q1fy29.xlsx (xlsx, 28KB)]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 May 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: CloudEdge — draft structure and pricing ask

Team — Samir sent the forecast and is ok with a 24-month horizon if we can make the numbers work. Key constraints: finance wants annualized billing + quarterly true-up; legal wants 60-day opt-out + audit/KMS attest.

Proposal idea (first pass):
- 24-month base commit covering ~70% of expected FY29 baseline (annualized invoiced at start of each year).
- Convertible-burst pool: X credits per quarter equal to 20% of committed baseline; credits burn for bursts up to a defined per-call cap.
- Conversion trigger: if running average utilization of committed baseline >= 90% over a trailing 90-day window, up to 50% of consumed burst credits can be converted into additional committed capacity at a pre-agreed uplift (e.g., +12% price).
- Auto-renew: 60-day opt-out, renews at contracted rates unless there’s a material change; SLA change notice 90 days.
- Invoice cadence: annualized with quarterly true-up and monthly usage reporting.

Attachments: proposed_term_sheet_v1.pdf, usage_forecast_Q3-Q4.xlsx, redwood_burst_policy.md

Questions for pricing: Marissa — does the conversion uplift (12%) look healthy vs risk? Ben — any technical limits on enforcing a 90-day lookback conversion safely? Rishi — can we get finance a simple pro-forma showing ARR impact?

Priya

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: CloudEdge — draft structure and pricing ask

Quick notes from SE perspective:
- Convertible-burst is feasible. We recommend burst credits throttle at token/sec per tenant and a per-request bucket to avoid noisy-neighbor impact.
- 90-day trailing average is fine; we’ll surface a daily utilization metric via the Console and alert at 80/90/95%.
- For conversion, capture the first 30 days of sustained utilization beyond the 90-day lookback as a buffer to avoid accidental conversions from transient spikes.
- We should include an explicit maximum convertible cap per quarter (e.g., 50% of burst credits) so we don’t expand capacity uncontrollably.

I’ll add language to the technical appendix and the proposed burst policy doc.

— Ben
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@cloudedge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, legal@cloudedge.io, finance@cloudedge.io
Date: Sat, 5 May 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal and scale — draft term summary and next steps

Samir — thanks for the fast turn. Attached is a concise term summary and the conversion appendix outlining thresholds, lookback windows, and max conversion caps. Highlights:
- 24-month base commit covering ~70% baseline; annualized billing at each contract anniversary with quarterly true-up.
- Convertible-burst pool sized at 20% of baseline per quarter; up to 50% of burned credits convertible after sustained utilization (90-day lookback + 30-day buffer); conversion price uplift: +12%.
- Auto-renew: 60-day opt-out; 90-day notice for SLA changes.
- Tech controls: token/sec caps, per-request buckets, Console alerts at 80/90/95%.

Next steps:
1) Samir — confirm you’re comfortable with the sizing assumptions in the attached forecast.
2) Marissa — will you confirm final pricing matrix and send to legal for a redline-ready term sheet?
3) We’ll open a DocuSign envelope for the term sheet after legal sign-off.

I’ll schedule a 30-minute sync next week to walk through the appendix with Ben if Samir’s team wants.

Best — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_term_sheet_v1.pdf (pdf, 42KB)]
